name: Tideglass Chandlery
description: A compact three-storey corner chandlery, approximately six metres of street frontage and seven metres deep. Cream salt-worn plaster between substantial warm oak corner posts on a pale limestone ground storey. The characteristic feature is a shallow octagonal corner bay carried by visible carved timber brackets, with a large round brass-rimmed tide dial mounted at the middle-floor bay (plain readable tide marks, no words); it is part of the wall rather than an unrelated tower. An elegant deep-teal hipped tile roof with two small dormers and a restrained copper ridge lantern, plus one narrow brick chimney. Ground-floor wraparound glazing displays a few large coils of rope, glass fishing floats and brass storm lanterns; a recessed green entrance, a simple lantern-shaped iron hanging sign and a rolled striped awning. Upper floors are occupied rooms, unevenly opened sage shutters, a small flower box, a mended curtain. Rear face: an oak loading door beneath a small tiled canopy, a compact upper delivery hatch with a short wall-mounted pulley arm, rain chain into a stone barrel and one narrow storage lean-to that is visible coherently in both views. The trade silhouette is tide clock plus light-filled lantern windows, not a lighthouse or monumental clock tower.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one detailed architectural concept sheet for the Rootward/Sparks seaside town, for eventual 3D modelling. TWO complete orthographic views of THE SAME SINGLE BUILDING, arranged side by side on plain warm ivory paper. It must be a specific believable town building, not a generic house and not a fantasy castle.
Input image 1: approved Guildhall Square STYLE/MATERIAL/CITY-DENSITY reference only. Input image 2: approved workshop lane OUTLINE/CRAFT/COASTAL-TOWN reference only. Do not copy either scene, beacon, guild hall, workshop or composition.
CAMERA AND LAYOUT: left panel shows FRONT plus RIGHT side, looking diagonally from the southeast. Right panel shows the BACK plus LEFT side, exactly 180 degrees around the same building. In both use orthographic parallel projection, 45-degree azimuth to the walls and about 31 degrees downward elevation from horizontal, the fixed game view. Vertical lines remain parallel; no lens/perspective convergence or distorted axes. Both views must show the same entire roof and all walls down to the foundations, no cutaways, with equal scale and lighting. Arrange generous blank space between the two silhouettes and at least 7 percent clear margins at every sheet edge. Neither roof, finial, chimney, hoist, window box, base nor rear accessory may be clipped.
STYLE: finely outlined warm painted 3D concept art like the supplied town. Strong readable roof/body forms, warm dark-brown contour lines, rich painterly material detail without noisy photorealism. Cream dressed limestone, weathered plaster, honey oak joinery, iron fittings, hand-laid roof tiles, modest brass/copper mechanisms and warm amber lamps. A cared-for, lived-in seaside trades town: salt wear low on masonry, patched shutters, practical gutters, believable doors/windows and occupied upper floors. The building could stand close to neighbouring buildings in a medium-sized dense town. Do not surround it with a floating cliff, sea diorama or a whole street. A thin restrained paving/foundation footprint below each building is enough.
CONTINUITY: exactly the same footprint, storey heights, roof ridge/gables, chimney positions, rear extension, wall openings and materials across the two views, rotated not mirrored or redesigned. Distinct front and back: shop front faces the street; deliveries, gutters and useful service details are at the rear. Supported balconies, roof loads and physically attached pipes/hoists. Keep decor subordinate to architecture. No people, robots, labels, lettering, dimension arrows, grid, title, watermark or modern cars. Signs may contain a simple pictorial trade emblem only. Landscape sheet, 1536x1024 or larger with both views equally detailed.
